# Pure scene-capture module: config parsing, validation and timing

The pure, browser-free core of the multi-scene capture feature (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC): parses and validates the scene-list JSON config, derives the watchable gym scene set, builds the per-scene capture plan (including the two 0.25 s fades), and formats the `--json` payload. No server, browser or Playwright imports — fully hermetic and unit-tested, consumed by the capture driver (sibling item). A shared browser-free registry of watchable gym scene keys mirrors the existing `CAPTURE_SCENARIOS` parity pattern (`scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs`) so the CLI pre-boot validation and the page-side director agree on the same set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Covers parent AC1.** A JSON config file specifies an ordered, arbitrary-length list of scenes; each entry carries a `target` (gym scene key), a `playMs` duration, a `captureMs` duration, and an optional `label`. The file is parsed and validated **before** any server/browser boots, failing fast with an actionable, non-zero-exit error for a missing/unreadable/malformed file, an unknown or unsupported `target`, an empty scene list, or a non-positive/non-numeric `playMs`/`captureMs` (mirroring the existing `--count` validation style).
- **Watchable target set.** The watchable gym scene set is derived from the discovered gym scenes minus the parameterised `GymFodderEnemies` and `GymLevel`; unknown or unsupported targets are rejected.
- **Scene-plan builder.** A pure builder computes per-scene `{ target, playMs, captureMs, startMs, endMs }`, inserting the two 0.25 s fades (`SCENE_FADE_MS = 250`) between consecutive scenes; exported, side-effect-free, deterministic.
- **JSON payload builder.** A pure builder reports per-scene timings, the total output duration and the output path.
- **Tests green.** The test-first sibling suite (`Tests: scene-capture config, timing and director keys`) passes; `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` declares the exported types.

## Key Files

- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` (new)
- `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` (new)
- `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` (sibling test item)
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs` (shared browser-free registry parity pattern)
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` (`parseCaptureCount` validation style reference)
- `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts` (discovered gym scene key convention, `Gym<Name>`)

## Minimal Implementation

1. New shared browser-free registry exported from this module: `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` (the discovered non-parameterised gym keys) and `SCENE_FADE_MS = 250`, following the `CAPTURE_SCENARIOS` parity pattern so the CLI and the director read one source of truth.
2. `parseSceneConfig` / `validateSceneConfig`: read + validate the JSON, reusing the `--count` error style; throw a typed error carrying an actionable message and a non-zero exit mapping.
3. Watchable-set validation against the registry; reject unknown/parameterised targets (`GymFodderEnemies`, `GymLevel`).
4. `buildScenePlan(scenes)`: per-scene `startMs`/`endMs` with the two fades between consecutive scenes; total duration.
5. `buildScenesPayload(...)`: the `--json` shape (per-scene timings + total duration + output path).
6. `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` type declarations matching the project's `.d.mts` convention.

## Dependencies

- Test-first sibling item (its tests define the contract).

## Deliverables

- Hermetic config/validation/planning module + types, consumed by the capture driver and the director.

# Intake Brief — AI bot does not know how to select upgrade in mini-boss reward screen (AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F)

## Problem statement

*"When the AI beats the mini boss it should be able to select an item from the
reward screen and carry on."* (original seed description)

When the demo/attract-mode bot defeats a mini-boss, `PlayScene.openMiniBossReward()`
opens the shared `MineralChoiceScene` overlay **without** the demo-only auto-select
parameters (`autoSelectMs` / `autoSelectIndex`) that the hold-full choice path
(`openMineralChoice`) passes. The overlay therefore waits forever for a human
selection, so the bot-driven demo run **stalls** on the mini-boss reward screen
instead of picking an upgrade/unlock and carrying on.

## Users

- **Attract/demo viewer** — *"As a viewer of the arcade-attract demo, I want the
  bot to pick a reward when it beats a mini-boss and keep playing, so the demo
  never freezes on the reward screen."*
- **Producer / marketing** — the demo doubles as a capture/regression harness;
  a demo that stalls mid-run looks broken and breaks auto-captures.
- **Balance/telemetry maintainer** — a stalled demo run never emits
  `choice_selected` for the reward, silently dropping reward telemetry.

## Acceptance Criteria (current choice-screen scope — producer approved quick fix, Q1=(a))

- **AC1 — Demo auto-select:** In demo mode (`PlayScene` started with
  `{ demo: true }`), when a mini-boss reward overlay opens it auto-selects an
  option after the existing human-like delay (`BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`
  from `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`), applies the choice through
  `selectMiniBossReward` (shared `applyMineralChoiceReward`), closes the overlay
  and resumes play — the demo never stalls on the reward screen. Verified by a
  demo-mode integration test mirroring the hold-full AC4 test in
  `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`. The selection routes through the
  overlay's shared 3-2-1 countdown before it is applied (the same cadence as the
  hold-full auto-select, AH-0MU55OBKS006TL4N) — there is no mini-boss-specific
  overlay or resume path.
- **AC2 — Random reward selection:** the auto-selected option is chosen
  **randomly** among the offered options (producer Q2=(b)), drawn from the
  run-seeded RNG so a given seed reproduces the same pick (repo RNG
  convention — deterministic per seed, no `Math.random()`); graceful `0 .. n-1`
  bounds handling for the offered array. Normal play never consults the
  preference.
- **AC3 — Normal play unchanged:** outside demo mode the reward overlay waits
  for a real pointer/keyboard selection; auto-select is demo-only
  (mirrors hold-full AC5 from AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB).
- **AC4 — Gym↔game parity preserved:** the demo bot seam is
  `PlayScene`-only (`getBotInput()` returns `null` in gyms), so the change adds
  no divergent gameplay copy; the shared `MineralChoiceScene` auto-select
  contract is reused, not duplicated.
- **AC5 — Documentation updated:** README *Attract / demo mode* paragraph and
  GDD §4.4.4 note the mini-boss reward auto-selects in demo mode (single tunable
  stays `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`).
- **AC6 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Reproduction

1. Start a demo run (`MenuScene → 👁 Watch Demo`, or 15 s menu inactivity) in a
   build with mini-bosses (shipped since v0.1.14).
2. Let the bot play until it defeats a level mini-boss.
3. Observed: the `MineralChoiceScene` overlay opens and the run pauses
   indefinitely — no selection is made, play never resumes.

## Constraints

- **Producer-approved scope (Q1=(a)): implement the quick fix on the current
  upgrade-or-unlock choice screen now.** The `blocked-by` dependency edge on
  AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD (wheel redesign) is removed so this item can be
  scheduled; that redesign must still preserve the "bot never stalls on the
  reward flow" property when it lands (related-work note).
- **Demo-only:** auto-select is gated on `demoMode`; normal play and gyms
  unchanged.
- **Single source of truth:** reuse the existing `autoSelectMs` /
  `autoSelectIndex` contract in `MineralChoiceScene` and the shared
  `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` tunable — no divergent overlay or magic numbers.
- **Data-driven choices:** the reward options are already built by the shared
  `buildUpgradeOptions` / `lockedWeaponIds` paths; the fix must not invent a
  parallel option model (AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH AC scope).

## Risks, assumptions and mitigations

- **Redesign risk:** the wheel redesign (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD) will replace the
  choice screen, potentially invalidating this fix when it lands. *Mitigation:*
  the fix is deliberately small and reuses the shipped hold-full auto-select
  pattern, so it is cheap to retire or adapt; the wheel item must preserve the
  "bot never stalls on the reward flow" property. Producer accepted this
  (Q1=(a) quick fix now).
- **Randomness/determinism risk:** a `Math.random()` selection would make demo
  replays non-deterministic, breaking seed-driven regression/telemetry runs.
  *Mitigation:* draw the random pick from the run-seeded RNG (same convention
  as bot press-duration jitter).
- **Scope-creep risk:** reward-flow redesign details (wheel odds, animation,
  additional reward surfaces, headless arena simulation) belong to the blocking
  item and the arena campaign work (AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A), not here. *Mitigation:*
  recorded as related work, not added to this item's ACs.
- **Assumption:** the demo bot can reach and beat a level mini-boss (already true
  — mini-bosses are gating wave spawns and the demo is a full-campaign run), so
  the stall is observable in the shipped demo.
- **Assumption:** outside demo mode the reward must keep waiting for a real
  selection — auto-select is demo-only, exactly as with the hold-full choice.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `openMiniBossReward()` (≈ L2986–3013) launches
  `MineralChoiceScene` with `origin: 'PlayScene-miniBoss'`, `options` and
  `onSelect: (i) => this.selectMineralChoice(i)` (which routes through
  `selectMiniBossReward` while the reward is open) — but **omits** the demo
  auto-select params.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `openMineralChoice()` (≈ L4493) is the working
  precedent: in demo mode it passes `autoSelectMs: BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`
  and `autoSelectIndex: this._preferredDemoChoiceIndex()`.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` already supports both parameters
  (`init()` defaults `autoSelectMs = 0`, `autoSelectIndex = 0` → auto-select
  disabled outside demo) — no scene change strictly required.
- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` L243 `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS = 900` — the single
  tunable shared by both surfaces.
- `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts` AC4/AC6 — canonical hold-full
  auto-select integration tests to mirror for the reward screen.
- Cosmetic: the overlay heading is hardcoded
  `'HOLD FULL — CHOOSE A POWER-UP'` even when launched from the mini-boss
  reward (origin `'PlayScene-miniBoss'`) — a visible copy bug on the reward
  screen (open question Q3; likely out of scope or a tiny separate item).

## Desired change

In `openMiniBossReward()`, when `this.demoMode`, pass
`autoSelectMs: BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` and a seeded **random**
`autoSelectIndex` (`0 .. options.length - 1`) to the overlay launch — mirroring
the hold-full path's demo params. Add a demo-mode integration test:
defeat/trigger a mini-boss reward, assert the overlay auto-selects after the
delay, applies the reward, closes the overlay and resumes play (extension of
`src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`). When the wheel redesign
(AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD) lands, its item must preserve the same
"bot never stalls on the reward flow" property.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `openMiniBossReward()`: add demo auto-select
  params with a seeded random reward pick (reviewer: reuse the run-seeded RNG,
  e.g. the same source as the bot's press-duration jitter, and bound the index
  to `0 .. miniBossRewardOptions.length - 1`); `selectMiniBossReward()`
  unchanged.
- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` — reuse `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` (already
  exported; no change expected).
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — no change expected (auto-select contract
  exists; heading copy out of scope per producer Q3=(b)).
- `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts` — demo mini-boss reward auto-select
  test (AC1/AC2), mirroring hold-full AC4 (open a reward via the same seam
  `openMiniBossReward`, assert auto-select + apply + resume).
- `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.4 — demo auto-select note
  (AC5).

## Related work

- **AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB** (completed) — Demo bot: human-like input limits +
  complete the hold-full upgrade choice; the original demo auto-select work
  (AC4/AC5 pattern) and this item's direct precedent.
- **AH-0MU55OBKS006TL4N** (completed) — Demo/attract auto-select routes through
  the countdown (selection → countdown → resume cadence).
- **AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4** (completed) — Bot prioritises extra lives in hold-full
  choice (the `_preferredDemoChoiceIndex` pattern; reward screen has no Extra
  Life so a mini-boss-specific preference is needed).
- **AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH** (completed) — Mini-boss reward: upgrade-or-unlock +
  locked pool (origin of the reward screen this bot fails to select on).
- **AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD** (open, **blocking**) — Mini-Boss rewards become
  valuable: the wheel-of-fortune redesign that replaces the choice screen.
- **AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A** (open) / **AH-0MVD1RIH2008YCNV** (blocked) — headless
  arena campaign + choice flow (mini-bosses not yet in the arena; out of scope
  here).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 — **Scope vs. wheel redesign** (source: producer Q1 reply, 2026-10-24):
  Map's earlier comment stated the reward screen is being replaced by the wheel
  (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD) and this screen-selection bug is "moot until that
  lands". Options considered: (a) fix the current choice screen now, (b) defer
  to the wheel, (c) re-scope to both. — **Answer (producer): "1. quick fix
  now" = (a).** The blocked-by dependency edge on AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD is
  removed so this item can proceed; the wheel item retains the
  bot-continuation requirement as a related-work note.
- Q2 — **Which option should the demo bot take on the reward screen?** Options:
  (a) first offered option (index 0), (b) upgrade highest-level owned weapon,
  (c) prefer unlocking a new weapon; intake recommended (a). — **Answer
  (producer): "2. random" = random option.** Final accepted answer: the demo
  auto-select picks randomly among the offered options, drawn from the
  run-seeded RNG for deterministic replay.
- Q3 — **Also fix the reward-screen heading copy?** `MineralChoiceScene`
  hardcodes 'HOLD FULL — CHOOSE A POWER-UP' even on the mini-boss reward
  origin; intake recommended out of scope. — **Answer (producer): "3. out of
  scope" = (b).** Heading copy not part of this item.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MV55OBKS006TL4N** – Demo/attract auto-select routes through the countdown (completed)
- **AH-0MVCRBISU006NUN5** – PlayScene mini-boss integration (completed)
- **AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB** – Demo bot: human-like input limits (W/A/D, reaction time) and complete the hold-full upgrade choice (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: able, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+324 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muxxq1mn002rxgb, 0mv03gxzq00801t4, 0mvcrbno6003e1ch, able, ac1 (+316 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: able, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+273 more)

# Test: wrapAware config plumbing

Test-first verification slice for the `wrapAware` parameter (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC1 + AC5). Pins the data-driven boolean's default, seed exclusions, CSV wiring and editor exposure **before** the implementation item lands, so the pipeline change is driven by failing tests.

## Goal

Pin the full config pipeline for `wrapAware`: default `true`, `march`/`centipede` seeded `false`, CSV persist + round-trip, editor-panel visibility.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test asserts a generic archetype resolves `wrapAware === true` when the field is absent from its seed config.
- Tests assert the `march` and `centipede` seed configs carry `wrapAware === false` (the explicit exclusion list).
- A CSV round-trip test asserts a `wrapAware` column persists and reloads through the config CSV path; a missing/empty value falls back to `true`.
- A test asserts the field is enumerable through the existing `EnemyConfig` editor/config plumbing without extra per-field admin.
- All tests pass deterministically (no wall clock, no RNG).

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts`
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts`
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts`
- `src/utils/csvEdit.ts`

# Data-driven force-field fields plus the pure resolver

**Parent:** AH-0MVJ8W4GE007OMNT (AC1).
**Depends on:** Resolver and codec contract tests (AH-0MVM8GQKI006B50M) (red contracts must exist first).

## Goal

As a balance engineer, I want per-archetype force-field strength to be
data-driven — which archetypes are shielded, from which level, and how the hit
count grows — so I can shape late-campaign difficulty from the CSV without
touching scene code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Data-driven per-archetype fields.** New `EnemyConfig` fields `forceFieldStartLevel`, `forceFieldStartHits`, `forceFieldMaxHits` added to types, CSV codec, defaults and rows, with the pure resolver.
- `EnemyConfig` gains `forceFieldStartLevel` (campaign level at which the
  archetype first gains a field; `0` = never shielded),
  `forceFieldStartHits` (field hits when it appears) and `forceFieldMaxHits`
  (field hits at the campaign maximum level), each with JSDoc stating the
  neutral default — `0` / `1` / `1` — so **every existing enemy is unshielded
  at level 1** and the shipped campaign is behaviourally unchanged at L1.
- `src/core/csv.ts` numeric codec reads/writes the three columns; absent
  columns default to `0`/`1`/`1`; `src/core/configDefaults.ts` seeds the
  defaults; the CSV header comments document each column.
- `src/core/enemyForceField.ts` (**new**) exports a pure, Phaser-free
  `enemyForceFieldHits(level, config)` implementing
  `clamp(round(lerp(startHits @ startLevel → maxHits @ maxLevel)), 0, 5)`,
  documented with the formula and reusing `clampLevel` from the landed
  `src/core/levelScaling.ts` (AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X) for level clamping.
- Shipped CSV rows carry per-archetype values with **subtle curve variations**
  (Q5): heavier archetypes (Tank, Harvester) get higher `forceFieldStartHits`
  /`forceFieldMaxHits` than light ones; start levels vary per archetype
  (some L2, others L3+); no archetype is shielded at L1.
- The red contract tests from the sibling test item go green; existing
  `csv`/`config`/`configStore` suites stay green; persisted blobs still load.
- Resolver is deterministic: same level + config ⇒ identical value.

## Documented assumptions

- Field strength is a pure function of `(level, config)` — no RNG.
- The campaign maximum level is 10 (`DEFAULT_LEVEL_SCALING_MAX_LEVEL`).

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — `EnemyConfig` fields.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts`, `src/core/configStore.ts`,
  `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — defaults, persisted-blob compatibility, rows.
- `src/core/csv.ts` — numeric codec + header comments.
- `src/core/enemyForceField.ts` — **new** resolver.

data.comment: Implementation notes: (1) Full-campaign mode via ArenaConfig.campaign reuses the exact game build — buildSequencedLevels(difficultyCurves, defaultCandidatePool(), { seed }) + the shared scaleCampaignLevelCounts seam (extracted from PlayScene.resolveCampaignLevels into src/core/levelScaling.ts so the game and the harness never diverge). (2) Progression is driven exclusively by the shared WaveManager (beginGame/planSpawns/onEnemyDestroyed); canonical wave_start/wave_cleared/level_cleared read the now-current wave/level exactly as runTelemetry records them. (3) AC4 boundary: boss_triggered ends the run; no boss/mini-boss entity simulated (mini-boss waves play their authored group composition) — documented in arena.ts module doc. (4) Wave shootEnabled gate honoured for campaign waves (GDD 2.4/2.5). (5) Spawner-delivered archetypes (ghosts/horde/centipede) are spawned and registered via registerDynamicSpawn; lane traffic uses the shared isNonBlockingHazard and never gates. (6) ArenaConfig.campaignLevels is a documented test seam (mirrors WaveManager injection) so the boss boundary is deterministically testable; production path always builds the shipped campaign.
